entities.text: S. Narsimha Reddy vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition No.18387 of 2023
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development appearing for respondent No.1, Sri M.A.K.Mukheed,
learned standing counsel for GHMC appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3.
With their consent, the writ petition is being taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. This writ petition has been filed seeking to declare the action of "Respondent Nos.2 and 3 and their subordinates in trying to lay road in the part of the land of the petitioners out of Ac.4-18 gts in Sy no 148/1, situated at Nanakramguda, Serilingampally, Ranga Reddy District without notice and without following due process of law either under Land Acquisition Act or under GHMC Act on the ground of widening of existing road leading from Khajaguda to Gopalpally of Ranga Reddy District as illegal apart from violation of provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 and

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
consequently direct the respondents not to lay the road in the land of the petitioners without following due process of law."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits petitioners and his family members are the absolute owner of the land to an extent of Ac.4- 18 gts, in Sy No.14/1, situated at Nanakramguda (v),
Serilingampally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District and further submits that on 28.06.2023, the respondent authorities started excavation work on the petitioners subject property for the purpose of widening of road.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that petitioners' forefather gave land for the purpose of road which is existing now and under the guise of expansion of the said road, the respondent authorities are illegal encroaching the petitioners land without issuing notice to the petitioners or without following due procedure contemplated under law and pray this Court to direct the respondent authorities to follow due process contemplated under law, if the petitioners property is required for any public purpose.
5.

Sri M.A.K.Mukheed, learned standing counsel for GHMC appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3,
submits that if the petitioners' property is required for widening of the road or for any public purpose, the respondent authorities will follow due process of law.

6. In view of the submission made by learned counsel on either side and upon perusal of the copies of photographs enclosed in the affidavit, it is evident that existing road is being digging with heavy machinery, hence, this Court deem it fit to direct the respondent Nos.2 and 3 to follow due process of law, if the petitioners property is required for any public purpose.
Till such time, respondent authorities are directed not to take coercive steps on the petitioners' subject land.
